## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle walk1 update, fused with a direct framebuffer scatter in walk2, can approach the machine's streaming bandwidth ceiling.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 11.334 at N=4000 (past the L1d spill at N≈949) to 8.039 at N=16000, reflecting overhead amortization at small N. Crossing the L2 spill at N≈60787 produces no knee: N=65000 gives 7.895 ns/p, and the curve stays flat through N=4M at 7.8 ns/p. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve — at q=0.25 the same fall-from-4000-to-16000 pattern appears (12.21 → 10.494) then flat at ~10.5 ns/p from N=65000 onward. No cache-spill knee is visible at either transition; the workload is compute/overhead-dominated, not cache-dominated.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 8.85 GB/s at N=4M, q=0.01 — 35% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The cell is overhead-bound: at 69 bytes/particle and 7.8 ns/p, pure streaming would require only 2.73 ns/p, so the cell spends ~2.85× the streaming time in computation. Bandwidth is flat across N from 16000 onward at each death rate, confirming no DRAM-bandwidth limitation. Death rate is the sole transition axis: q=0.05 holds ~8.3 GB/s (33%), q=0.25 drops to 6.58 GB/s (26%), as the branchy respawn/scatter path consumes more cycles per particle.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized walk1 component-wise within one particle: `ldur q16` loads 4 floats, `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` rearranges them, `fmul.4s v7, v18, v2` and `fadd.4s v7, v16, v7` apply the update across 4 lanes, and `stur q7` writes back. A gather-style `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x11]` loads a single component into one lane. Walk2's fused scatter is entirely scalar: `ldp s0, s1` loads position, then `fcvtzs`/`csel`/`fcmp` clamp coordinates, and three `ldrb`/`strb` pairs per pixel write RGB bytes to the framebuffer via `bfi`-computed offsets. The 17 `strb` and 13 `ldrb` instructions, plus 18 `csel` and 6 `ccmp` for bounds checks, dominate the instruction mix and explain why bandwidth caps at 35% — the scatter's byte-granular random writes cannot stream.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell never exceeds 8.85 GB/s (35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, and drops to 6.58 GB/s (26%) at q=0.25. Walk1 auto-vectorizes with `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s`, but the fused scatter's scalar byte stores (`strb`) and branchy bounds-checking (`csel`, `ccmp`, `tbnz`) dominate runtime, preventing any approach to the streaming ceiling regardless of death rate or N.
